report.summary: The observable fault is in the frontend-proxy tier. In the astronomy-shop namespace the Deployment frontend-proxy was updated (generation 2 / revision 2) and rolled out at 11:51:56-11:51:58 with an unchanged image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy): the old ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 carries a single FRONTEND_HOST=frontend, while the new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 carries a second, trailing FRONTEND_HOST=localhost appended to the same env list. At query time the new pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-m7t8b is not ready and its container has restartCount 3 with current state terminated reason OOMKilled (exit 137), the Deployment reports MinimumReplicasUnavailable, and the frontend-proxy Service has no ready address at all (its only address is in notReadyAddresses), whereas frontend and the other 22 services each have a ready address. The load generator is the customer-facing signal: the HighRequestErrorRate alert for GET / in astronomy-shop is pending with a failure ratio of 1.00, locust_requests_fail_ratio read 0.348 at 11:52:00, and the load-generator's fetcher log at 11:51:52 lists HTTPError('503 Server Error') for GET / and for many /api/* paths. The most consistent mechanism is that FRONTEND_HOST=localhost makes Envoy proxy the frontend cluster to its own 127.0.0.1:8080 listener, producing self-referential request handling (503s) and memory growth that ends in OOMKill under the 65Mi limit; that mechanism is a hypothesis, because no in-window Envoy 503 line or OOM event was captured. Feature-flag fault injection is ruled out: every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap has defaultVariant "off". Conclusion is partial because the deployment change and the pod's failure are established but the fault as declared (in-window 503s caused by the new pod) and the actor that changed the Deployment were not observed.

claims.text: The Deployment astronomy-shop/frontend-proxy has generation 2 and deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, and at 11:53:19 its status is Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 (message: 'ReplicaSet "frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4" has successfully progressed.').
The superseded ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (now replicas 0) defines exactly one FRONTEND_HOST env entry, value "frontend", in its container env list.

The current ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 (replicas 1) has the same FRONTEND_HOST=frontend entry and, in addition, a trailing duplicate FRONTEND_HOST=localhost appended at the end of the same container env list, with an unchanged image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy.

Rollout events show the Deployment frontend-proxy scaling new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 from 0 to 1 at 11:51:56 (pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-m7t8b created and scheduled at 11:51:56) and scaling the old ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 from 1 to 0 at 11:51:58, killing pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-96qpw at 11:51:58.

At 11:53:38 the container frontend-proxy of pod frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-m7t8b is ready=false with restartCount 3; its current state is terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 (finishedAt 11:53:30) and its lastState is terminated with reason Error and exitCode 137 (finishedAt 11:52:59).

At 11:54:35 the Service endpoints for frontend-proxy list no ready address; its only address 10.244.234.186 appears under notReadyAddresses, while frontend (10.244.7.217) and the other 21 application Services each have a ready address (e.g. cart 10.244.234.188, checkout 10.244.125.30, payment 10.244.125.18).

The alerting rule HighRequestErrorRate for the load generator in namespace astronomy-shop is pending for method GET, name "/", instance load-generator.astronomy-shop:9646, with value 1.00 (elevated failure ratio) at evaluation 11:51:26.
locust_requests_fail_ratio for instance load-generator.astronomy-shop:9646 (job locust-astronomy-shop, namespace astronomy-shop) read 0.34831460674157305 at 11:52:00.

The locust-fetcher log line ingested at 11:51:52 lists HTTPError('503 Server Error: Service Unavailable for url: /') with 10 occurrences, plus 503s for /api/cart (GET 4, POST 1), /api/products/*, /api/data/, /api/product-reviews/* and /api/recommendations?productIds=*.

Every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (including adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse, adHighCpu, adManualGc) has defaultVariant "off".

Before the rollout the storefront path was serving successfully: spans sampled for frontend-proxy between 11:51:48 and 11:51:55 carry status tag http.status_code 200 (e.g. trace 6abf41dc34842e802ef86124c00fbbbb: frontend-proxy GET 200, frontend POST /api/checkout 200), and pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-96qpw logged envoy 'all clusters initialized' at 11:51:05.

The 503 errors reported by the fetcher were ingested at 11:51:52, i.e. about four seconds before the new ReplicaSet was scaled up at 11:51:56, so at least part of that 503 burst is not explained by the new pod; a startup-phase explanation (environment installed from 11:50:59, first locust samples from 11:51:10) cannot be excluded from this evidence.

A flagd feature-flag fault injection is not the cause: all flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap are enabled for evaluation but every one of them has defaultVariant "off", so no ad/cart/payment/product-catalog/email/LLM fault variant was in effect.

Root cause: the Deployment frontend-proxy was patched to add a trailing FRONTEND_HOST=localhost env override (image unchanged, generation 2). Envoy's envoy.tmpl.yaml is rendered with envsubst, so the frontend cluster points at the proxy's own listener 127.0.0.1:8080, producing self-referential request handling that returns 503 to the load generator and unbounded memory growth (each hop adds headers), ending in OOMKill under the container's 65Mi limit and leaving the frontend-proxy Service with no ready endpoint.

A separate telemetry-pipeline problem exists: the otel-collector-agent pods log "Post http://otel-collector:4318/v1/metrics: dial tcp 10.96.18.103:4318: connect: connection refused" and "flush: dial tcp 10.96.103.100:9200: connect: connection refused" (opensearch exporter), and events record readiness-probe failures on otel-collector-agent-kt6z7/rxcbl/t7qcw plus a FailedMount on otel-collector-agent-kt6z7 for volume opentelemetry-collector-configmap.

The otel-collector Service in astronomy-shop selects the agent-collector pods themselves (selector component=agent-collector), so the agents' export target otel-collector:4318 resolves back to the agents, which explains the repeated connection refused; this affects telemetry delivery only and is not evidence of the storefront 503s.

gaps: The declared fault itself was not observed inside the authorized window: no Envoy 503/upstream-error log line and no OOM event from the new frontend-proxy pod fall before 11:52:10, and fetch_pod_logs reported that all 242 readable lines of frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-m7t8b lie after the window (crash times 11:52:59 and 11:53:30 are outside it).

Who or what changed the frontend-proxy Deployment to generation 2 is unknown: the change-history integration is not available in this Run, so the actor and the exact change time between 11:51:01 and 11:51:56 could not be verified.

Whether the duplicated env var actually wins over the earlier FRONTEND_HOST=frontend at container runtime (ordering/lookup semantics of duplicate env entries and envsubst) was not verified; no rendered envoy.yaml for the new pod was readable.

Prometheus history in this target was effectively limited to roughly the last minute of the window (e.g. kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and locust series returned samples only from about 11:51:10-11:52:10), so no error-rate or latency baseline exists and no latency trend can be stated; traces_span_metrics_calls_total for namespace astronomy-shop returned no rate data over 10:52-11:52 and only a handful of series (accounting, ad, currency, email, frontend-proxy) at 11:52:00.

Error status for the other services inside the window remains unknown: traces_search_by_tags error=true on frontend (11:45-11:52:10) and the 503 tag search on frontend-proxy matched nothing, and traces_search for checkout (11:51:50-11:52:10) returned no traces; these empty results show only that those queries matched nothing, not that those services were error-free.

The load-generator's 503 burst includes errors ingested at 11:51:52, before the rollout; whether those were startup-phase failures of the freshly installed namespace could not be separated from the injected fault.
The otel-collector/opensearch export failures were observed only in agent logs and events; whether they also lose spans or metrics that would have shown the in-window error rate was not determined.
next_steps: Compare the live Deployment frontend-proxy pod template with the Helm-rendered chart value (single FRONTEND_HOST=frontend) and, if the trailing FRONTEND_HOST=localhost is not chart-defined, revert that env entry and confirm the rollout returns a ready pod.
Read frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4-m7t8b's current and previous container logs for the 11:52:44-11:53:30 crash windows to confirm whether Envoy was looping requests to itself before the OOMKill.
Inspect the rendered envoy.yaml inside the running frontend-proxy container (envsubst output for the frontend cluster) to confirm whether the upstream resolved to 127.0.0.1:8080.
Once a ready endpoint exists, re-check locust_requests_fail_ratio and the HighRequestErrorRate rule for GET / to verify the 503s stop.
Separately investigate the otel-collector Service selector (component=agent-collector) and the opensearch exporter refusals so that spanmetrics and logs are complete for future baselines.
